answer.answer:
The goal was met. Five settings, each on a different scene, failed on every repeat, and their 90% ranges lie above 0.5. They are S18 (-0.1 m, 1.2x), S13 (+0.1 m, 1.2x), S21 (-0.5 m, 1.0x), S24 (+0.3 m, 0.8x) and S26 (-0.5 m, 1.4x). The failures are either a lane change into a vehicle alongside or a drift off the road. Usually the ego moves the same way the bias points. The triage blames VaVAM's policy for every failure.

Failure does not need a large bias or a high speed. Settings at 0 to ±0.1 m and speeds from 0.6x to 1.4x also failed. So these are best read as scene-specific weaknesses that a small shift brings out, not as a clear bias-by-speed threshold. In many of these runs the policy also ignored the route command.

Each confirmed rate rests on only a few repeats, so the ranges only show it is above about one half, not how high it is. S13, S24 and S26 rest entirely on failures flagged as possible simulator artifacts, because the ego ended far from the recorded path. The triage reads those as the policy's own steering, with the camera view clean before the departure.

findings.claim: Scene 187e6244 at -0.5 m, 1.0x: every run failed the same way. Under a STRAIGHT command the ego changed lanes to the right, cutting into the vehicle alongside in that lane (actor 3). That matches the direction of the bias. No artifacts were flagged.

Scene 1b7d131a at -0.5 m, 1.4x: every run drifted right and went off the road into the trees and guardrail at highway speed, while the command and route bent left. No actors were involved. All runs carry the artifact flag, but the triage reports a clean camera view before the departure. In the same scene, a single run at +0.5 m, 0.6x went off the road to the left, again following the bias.

Scene 09a95ffa: at +0.1 m, 1.2x every run changed lanes to the left into a vehicle coming up alongside (actor 28). At -0.1 m with the same speed, and at -0.2 or -0.3 m at 1.0x, nothing failed. Here the sign of the bias decides it, not its size. All the failures at +0.1 m carry the artifact flag because the ego ended about 4.9 m off the recorded path.

Scene 19f339ba at +0.3 m, 0.8x: every run slowed hard and steered left against a RIGHT command until it left the road at the median. Rear contacts from following traffic happened during the slowdown but did not cause the failure. A low speed does not make this scene safe: +0.2 m at 0.6x failed in most of its runs, and a single run at +0.3 m, 1.4x also left the road. One run at -0.1 m, 1.0x did not fail. These failures carry the artifact flag.

Scene 0cf6368d (slow, queued traffic) at -0.1 m, 1.2x: every run failed, but not all by leaving the lane. Some runs crept into the stopped lead vehicle in the ego's own lane without braking. Others steered out of the lane into an adjacent vehicle. Single runs at -0.3 m and -0.2 m also failed, so this scene fails across the settings tried.

Scene 096988dd fails with little or no bias. At +0.1 m, 1.0x and at 0.0 m, 1.2x every run drifted left into the pickup alongside (actor 41). A single run at -0.5 m, 1.0x went right into actor 3. A single run at 0.0 m, 0.6x did not fail. These runs hint that speed at or above the recorded speed is enough here, and that the bias sets the direction.

Scene 05f35348 at -0.3 m, 1.0x: every run braked hard and drifted right off the road onto the shoulder, all flagged as possible artifacts. A single run at -0.2 m did not fail, but a single run at 0.0 m, 0.8x did fail: an overtaking car clipped the ego after it braked hard for no visible reason. That makes a clean bias threshold here doubtful.

Single-run hints on other scenes: 0ce6f2a3 at -0.5 m, 0.8x and 12855a41 at -0.3 m, 0.8x each failed in their one run, the first by going off the road to the right and the second by drifting right into a vehicle alongside. 12855a41 at 0.0 m, 1.2x did not fail. 023b7fcc at +0.1 m, 1.4x failed in most runs by going off the road with no actor involved, all flagged as possible artifacts. Its single run at -0.3 m, 0.6x did not fail.

Many of the failures happen where the route command disagrees with the ego's path: the policy holds straight or steers against a LEFT or RIGHT command. That cause is mixed in with the effect of the plan bias.

open: How high the confirmed rates are. Each confirmed setting rests on a few repeats, so its range only shows it is above about one half. More repeats of S18, S13, S21, S24 and S26 would narrow it.

Whether the failures flagged as possible artifacts (all of S13, S24, S26 and S3, and most of S2 and S23) are the policy's or the renderer's. Reruns at the same settings with a closer look at the video, or with a smaller bias that keeps the ego nearer the recording, would help settle it.

How much is caused by the bias and how much by the scene or the route command. Baseline runs at 0.0 m, 1.0x on the five confirmed scenes, plus bias-sign flips (e.g. +0.5 m at 1.0x on 187e6244, and -0.1 m and +0.1 m at 1.0x on 09a95ffa), would separate the two.
Whether there is a speed effect at all. Failures appeared from 0.6x to 1.4x. Sweeping speed at a fixed bias on one scene, e.g. 096988dd at 0.0 m across 0.6x to 1.4x with repeats, would map it.
The single-run failures (S5, S6, S14, S15, S16, S17, S19, S25, S27) are hints, not rates. Each needs repeats.
Scenes 0dbb91dd and 054b5901 were never run, and most of the 9 × 5 grid was not explored, so harder cases may exist.
Near misses were not ranked, and no lane departure that ended without contact or leaving the road was measured.
One run was not kept (RE-RUN) and one was halted (-0.5 m, 0.8x on 1b7d131a). The halted setting remains untested.
